_comment: Every exception to the content guard, with a written reason. Reviewed at each milestone. An entry here is a deliberate decision, not a bypass. The pattern across all of them is the same: these are NEGATIVE uses — the site saying it will not publish a claim, or the Appendix B safeguard warning the reader to verify. A positive claim would not qualify.

exceptions.reason: Appendix B safety note, verbatim and mandated. It instructs the reader to confirm working-load limits against manufacturer documentation — the opposite of asserting one.
Appendix B safety note, verbatim. States that a marking may not establish a CERTIFIED working-load limit. A warning, not a claim.
The schema field name `certifications`, locked to an empty array. Its presence in the source is the lock that PREVENTS publishing a certification.
safety.withheldClaims audit record: states the 3T marking is NOT presented as a working-load limit. Internal record, never rendered to a page.
safety.withheldClaims audit record listing what is withheld pending manufacturer documentation. Never rendered.
safety.withheldClaims audit record: tensile strength is withheld pending documentation.
safety.withheldClaims audit record: marine certification is withheld; 'marine use' is published as a possible application only.
The Product Safety page's whole purpose is to name what Feytom withholds and why (§8.6). Every occurrence is inside a sentence stating the claim is NOT published until documented.
